content: S1: the loop owns dispatch, so one flow of work replaces the orchestration (plans/task-flow.md S1). The wake landed 2026-10-03 (9aef0cbb): a write that makes a row ready wakes its headless holder, and the handoff needs no verb of its own. Gate: one fan-out run by hand, on the loop alone.

records.result: Landed 2026-10-03. The run's end now takes its members: end_spent_runs hangs off the same TodoUpdated arm as the wake, ends a run whose rows are all gone through the one end_session (extracted from the stop path), and only ever ends headless members the run spawned, so a session a person sits in is never reaped. Checked: 394 kcode-app-core server tests pass, a_spent_run_takes_only_the_sessions_it_spawned pins the selection, clippy clean on the changed files. What I did not check: the live fan-out, which is t3 and waits for the next build. Also correcting this row: the idle members seen on 2026-10-03 sat there while the run still had open rows, which is by design (a member's session outlives its turn so it can be handed more rows); the case fixed here is the run whose rows are all closed leaving its members alive forever.

Landed in four commits, 1,915 lines gone: 9ddcd773 the action, 37c56551 the card, 738c8784 the driver and its policies, 5e5813c8 the claim, with cf559947 for the formatting the scripted deletions broke. Nothing else in the tree named the driver, and the file compiles with no dead code.

Subsumed by S1b, not done separately. auto_assign_claims and its 15 s TTL are used only by the assign path's target selection (comm_control.rs:279 and :478, both inside the assign handlers), so deleting the verbs deletes the claim map with them. Nothing else claims a target: the loop picks the rows the session holds, and the holder write is the model's.

Subsumed by S1b, not done separately. The dispatch-time liveness predicate is the inlined rule inside next_dispatch (comm_control.rs:355), which S1b deletes. The sweep's predicate (salvage_dead_assignees, swarm.rs:567) is then the only copy, so the disagreement the braid note recorded resolves by deletion rather than by a new assignee_is_dead.

Landed in five commits, 4,065 lines gone: ced7e526 the three tool actions with the test file they lived in, fbd12d86 retry and wake (the assign request's last tool caller), da58d37e the two flags the verbs owned, d150dba1 the wire requests, the request arms, the handlers and the whole machinery behind them, da1669b6 the test scaffolding left over. S1h and S1i went with it as scoped: auto_assign_claims had no other user, and the dispatch-time liveness predicate was the rule inlined in next_dispatch, so the sweep's predicate is now the only copy. comm_control.rs is 1,426 lines to 28. resolve_run_plan_concurrency stayed: its only surviving caller is plan_status_budget_line, so it belongs to S1c. Gate: kcode-app-core 875 tests and kcode-protocol 74 green, fmt and both ratchets green, check_guardrails failing only the pre-existing clippy double_must_use class, test.sh full green bar the three known session_flow e2e reds. What I did not check: the live fan-out, which is S1k and waits for the next build.

Landed in seven commits, -5,748 +250 lines. S1c-1a e2f92835: the three graph verbs and the dag engine they were the only door to (comm_graph.rs, kcode-plan/src/dag, bridge::seed_specs/to_task_graph/status_from_plan, is_composite, NodeKind moved to bridge because live_turn names one; the dag e2e died with its handlers and the swarm tool's schema lost its two open-world payloads, so it became strict-eligible on OpenAI routes). S1c-1b 9a51b186: the driver's pick policy in kcode-plan (the three next_*_runnable_item_id, explicit_task_blocked_reason, is_unblocked, AssignmentAffinities and assignment_affinities_for_task) which S1b had orphaned behind pub. S1c-2 9747c4d7: status, summary, plan_status, read_context, resync_plan and list, with comm_sync 513 to 248, comm_format 674 to 222, AgentStatusSnapshot, and the action names now one ACTIONS const the schema enum and the unknown-action error both read. S1c-3 52799b28: report and both report channels, the three status writers collapsed to one, the spawn reminder, and the turn-end latest_assistant_text_after read. S1c-4 a09dcf24: the assignment suffix (hydrate_assignment, upstream_context, combine_assignment_text), HandoffArtifact with it, and bridge renamed kind.rs since there is no dag to bridge. ff3bd8dc: two stale name tables (the log filter's read-only kinds, the TUI's tool-call arm, which was also a duplicate of the arm below it). fe1528f3: the plan's decisions and the ledger's price.

Decisions taken: list is in (the keep list is four actions and its fact is the row's holder); the tldr rule goes in S1f, not here, because four of its five callers went and the one message verb is the last; the coordinator notification stays but keeps only the lifecycle fact, since the close is the report now, and a cycle refusal is the one guard the dag writer had that nothing has now.

Kept by name, because a deletion waits for its last caller: Request::CommReadContext with handle_comm_read_context and CommContextHistory (the await path reads a member's transcript for its report, S1e); comm_sync::member_runtime_extras (the shared-context view, S1f); SwarmMember::latest_completion_report (write-never now, read by the await path and the channel-members copy).

Gate: check_guardrails all green except the pre-existing clippy double_must_use class in kcode-provider-core (untouched by this step); kcode-app-core 852, kcode-protocol 66, kcode-swarm-core 11, kcode-plan 8, kcode-base 1096, kcode-tui 1759/1760 where the one red is the documented ambient-environment flake (it passes with the shell's KCODE_OPENROUTER_* unset and is a provider-suggestion test this change cannot reach). What I did not check: the live fan-out, which is S1k and waits for the next build.

Landed in three commits, all of them deletions plus one rule change: 77869d25 (cleanup and the last member listing), b29be947 (stop ends the run's subtree, force gone), 28a8b6b1 (the departure reads the list from the session that held the rows). Done: cleanup with its helpers (cleanup_swarm_workers, cleanup_candidate_session_ids, stop_swarm_sessions with WorkerCleanupOutcome, comm_format's two cleanup helpers); Request::CommList with handle_comm_list, since fetch_swarm_members was its last sender (ServerEvent::CommMembers stays, channel_members answers with it); comm_sync's roster extras, which were the list handler's and not the shared-context view's, so comm_sync is 513 to 111 and holds only the await path's read; stop now reads the target's subtree off the spawn edge and ends it deepest first, force and swarm_stop_allowed_by_owner are gone, and the tool's stop line is one line with the rule in the schema. Corrections to what the row said: stop never called stop_swarm_sessions (cleanup did), and the roster extras were not S1f's.

Decisions taken (the user's): delete force, which removes the peer stop and keeps the root's revoke through ancestry; keep the reply one line and put the subtree rule in the schema, since Done carries no count. The D4 fix was needed exactly because a subtree stop empties the run: the release read the list from the live member map after the member was removed, so a run's last session released nothing and its rows stayed held by a corpse. end_session, the rename path and the disconnect path now run the departure before the removal; the two terminal-member GC passes still remove first, deliberately, because their rows were released at death and widening the expiry window would buy nothing.

Not built and not tested, by the user's call: S1 builds and tests once, at S1k, which is now noted in the plan. So the first compile of S1c and S1d is the gate, and what I did not check is that they compile and that the touched suites pass.

records.result: Landed. kind_of (live_turn.rs) is the one reader of rule 8 and row_is_ready now requires it, so a row with no kind, or a blank one, is not ready: it neither wakes a headless holder (wake_ready_owners filters on row_is_ready) nor gets picked (next_held_ready_row's ready closure calls the same predicate). The clause sits in the pick, not in the tool's write, so typing the kind later is the intended recovery. Swept up: three loop tests that built kindless rows now give them a kind (server::tests' live_run builder, client_lifecycle_tests' standing-default rows), because rule 8 makes a kind a precondition of any row the loop can work. New: a_row_with_no_kind_is_not_ready, the_pick_skips_a_row_with_no_kind. Checked: cargo clippy -p kcode-app-core --all-targets -D warnings clean; scripts/test.sh crate kcode-app-core, 832 passed, 0 failed. What I did not check: the live wake on a socket, which the by-hand fan-out covers for the kinded path.

what_i_did_not_check: a live worker's first message (the smoke list's fan-out or G2)

records.result: Landed. row_turn_message (live_turn.rs) appends `kind: <kind>` after the content when kind_of is Some, so the turn a woken holder receives carries the row's own words and its kind, which is the payload the model names. It reads kind_of, the same predicate the pick uses, so the message cannot disagree with seedability. the_message_carries_the_rows_own_words now asserts the kind line. Checked: cargo clippy -p kcode-app-core --all-targets -D warnings clean; scripts/test.sh crate kcode-app-core, 832 passed, 0 failed. What I did not check: a live worker's first message, which the smoke list's fan-out or G2 would show.

Landed. One limit: agents.swarm_max_concurrent_agents, 32 by default and 0 to switch it off, counting the live spawned members of a run, read in the one place a member is created (ensure_spawn_coordinator_swarm, comm_session.rs). Deleted the hard constant MAX_SWARM_MEMBERS = 1000 with its re-export, its check and its message, the live_member_count it existed for, the two clamps, and the test spawn_rejected_when_member_limit_reached; terminal_members_do_not_consume_spawn_capacity keeps its meaning with a literal filler count. Done as part of the refresh. Every open item in plans/task-flow.md now has a row: S1's leftovers (the two kind rows landed, the orphaned store functions are t25), the bound (t12, landed), S2 t15, S3 t16, S4 t17, S5a t18, S5b t19 (landed), D2 t20, G1 t22, G2 t23, G3 t24, and this row. Nothing open in the lane lacks a home, and the rows hold the work while the plan holds the design. Checked: the row list against the plan's headings by hand (2026-10-04).

Landed. The holder check that lived only in close_row_on_disk moved into close_row (kcode-base/src/todo.rs), which now takes the closing session's id: a row naming a different holder is refused, and taking a row is a write, so the user's session keeps its power by claiming first. close_row_on_disk, claim_row_on_disk and expand_row_on_disk are gone, all three with no caller since S1c deleted the plan engine; kcode-plan's MAX_PLAN_ITEMS went with them, its last user gone. Tests: a_run_closes_only_a_row_it_still_holds became a_close_refuses_a_row_held_by_another_session on the in-memory close_row, a_claim_and_a_release_move_the_holder_on_the_row became a_release_frees_the_row, and the three close_row call sites in the store's tests pass a session id. The plan's S1 leftover note records the move. Checked: cargo fmt clean; clippy -p kcode-base -p kcode-plan -p kcode-app-core --all-targets -D warnings clean; scripts/test.sh crate kcode-base PASS and crate kcode-app-core PASS (action log, exit 0). What I did not check: a live close across two sessions on a socket.

content: S2 one view: the server forwards the rows a session may work to that session's client (the BusEvent::TodoUpdated the server folds into the member cache today, server.rs:2065), and the client renders one surface from it, absorbing the inline card, the side-panel page, the pinned band, the info pips and the gallery's at-a-glance role. Deletes four renderers, four caches and fifteen file reads. Gate: the four old surfaces gone; a live TUI check on a run with two workers showing progress, holder and status; the client suite.

S3 one status (waits on S2): liveness becomes the holder's own session status plus one predicate for a holder that can never return; delete SwarmMemberRuntime.todo_items (the third copy of a session's rows), the four member shapes and the third event log. Gate: the member cache gone, one predicate decides liveness, the TUI reads the typed status.

S4 the record is the words: the artifact form goes and a record is {id, result}; the close's discipline (what proves it, what it showed, what it did not check) lives in the close instruction. Deletes the tool's close_artifact builders and the engine's writers. Gate: one record shape, no confidence/findings fields.

S5a status, priority and group leave TaskItem, with the four status vocabularies they keep alive (kcode-plan's five helpers, kcode-base's canonical_todo_status and its wrappers, the TUI's normalize_plan_status_for_todo, status_badge and the second priority_rank). Afterwards readiness is blocked_by empty and liveness comes from the member, not the item. Gate: the three fields gone and the vocabularies with them.

D2 the swarm/comm condense: the SwarmState handle pair is rebuilt as a literal at each request arm and threaded to ~40 functions; give the swarm state its one owner and delete the pair. This is the work that gates plans/server-shape.md H2. Gate: no SwarmState literal at a request arm.
G1 restore the two size ratchets in scripts/check_guardrails.sh and re-baseline both with --update; they are paused with the reason at the call site.

G2 the one live kcode run probe against its own socket, in a scratch repo, run by the user: the permission (a granted turn continues, a wake does not) and the poke's removal (no client continuation; every non-retryable error gets the short budget). It is the lane's landing proof, so it runs when the list is done, not per step.

G3 the work list gets its user doc under docs/user/ (tasks.jsonl at the repo root, the todo tool's actions, the close's required result), and the model's half: the tool description names where the list lives, since the first fan-out run's root hunted the filesystem for it. Waits until the shape stops moving at S5.
